what: The `db` factory ran without a database URL: no `url` thunk and no `DB_URL`.
fix: Set `DB_URL`, or pass a `url` thunk to `db()`.

what: `repos({ withTx })` used `withTx` as a repository name. `withTx` is the helper that rebinds every repos set.
fix: Rename the repository.

what: `reader(repo, [name])` named something that is not a method of the repository.
fix: List only method names of the repository.

what: `sessionPool.connect()` ran while `DB_URL` is a known transaction pooler and no direct URL is set. Through the pooler, LISTEN hears nothing and a session lock outlives its owner.
fix: Set `DB_DIRECT_URL`, or pass a `directUrl` thunk to `db()`.

what: The database URL does not fit the plugin: a `postgres:` URL given to `db()` from `@arki/db/libsql/dot`, or a SQLite URL (`file:`, `libsql:`, `:memory:`) given to the pg driver of `@arki/db/dot`. The wrong driver would fail later, with a less clear error.
fix: Use the plugin that matches the URL, or fix the URL.

what: Every attempt failed with a retryable SQLSTATE (`40001` or `40P01`).
fix: Shorten the transaction, touch rows in a fixed order, or raise `retries` (at most 10).

what: `isolation` is not `serializable`, `retries` is not a whole number from 0 to 10, or an option key is unknown.
fix: Fix the options. Nothing is clamped.

what: A transactional procedure was called with a context that is already inside a transaction.
fix: Open one transaction per call. Call the usecase directly instead.

what: `transact` is not the last `.use()`, or `implement` was not given `transactionalProcedureConfig`.
fix: Put `.use(transact)` last and pass `transactionalProcedureConfig` to `implement`.

what: The transactional handler returned a stream.
fix: Return plain data. Stream from another procedure.

what: The database handed to the transaction helper is already a transaction.
fix: Pass the root database.

what: The database is SQLite on a driver other than libSQL (bun:sqlite, node:sqlite, better-sqlite3, sqlite-proxy). Those commit when an async callback returns, not when it settles, so a throw after an `await` keeps its writes.
fix: Open the database with `createLibsqlDb` from `@arki/db/libsql`, or `db()` from `@arki/db/libsql/dot`.

what: Two features export a schema entry under the same key, so one would hide the other.
fix: Rename one table or relation export so each key is unique across features.

what: A projection was declared without a name.
fix: Pass a non-empty `name` when you declare the projection.

what: A projection was declared without the events it reads.
fix: List at least one event in the projection `events`.

what: Two features define a relation under the same key.
fix: Rename one relation key so each is unique across features.

what: The first connection or `LISTEN` of a listener failed (no free client, permission denied, no `LISTEN` support). Nothing retries: the start rejects with an `UnexpectedFailure` whose `failure` is this value and whose `cause` is the raw pool error. (`WakeListener` in `@arki/journal` is `Unlisten | Promise<Unlisten>`, so the start cannot return a failure without changing that contract.)
fix: Check the pool, the credentials and that the server supports `LISTEN`, then start the listener again.

what: A live process already owns this data directory.
fix: Close its existing handle or choose another data directory.

what: The owner lock kept changing throughout the bounded acquisition attempts.
fix: Wait for competing openers to finish before opening the directory again.

what: Closing resources or releasing their owner lock could not be confirmed.
fix: Inspect the private causes; retain ownership until the handle is confirmed closed.

what: The filesystem rejected the selected local database path or operation.
fix: Choose a writable directory with the required filesystem permissions.

what: The filesystem temporarily could not perform the local database operation.
fix: Restore filesystem capacity or availability before trying again.

what: Migration source files could not be read or decoded.
fix: Inspect the private cause and restore the generated migration directory before running again.

what: The current migration bookkeeping state could not be read.
fix: Restore database access and inspect its bookkeeping before deciding what to apply.

what: The native migrator did not confirm completion; schema or bookkeeping changes may exist.
fix: Reconcile the database schema and migration bookkeeping before explicitly running again. Do not retry blindly.

what: A session feature was given a pooled URL and no direct one.
fix: Set `DB_DIRECT_URL` (or pass `directUrl`) to the host's direct URL.

what: A stored value cannot be read as the column's type: Postgres `infinity`, a BC date, malformed text, or SQLite milliseconds that are NaN or out of range. Drizzle's `fromDriver` cannot return a failure, so the column codecs throw this as an `UnexpectedFailure` (`error.failure` is this value); the raw `RangeError` is its `cause`.
fix: Repair or remove the stored value, or read the column as text and handle the special value yourself.

what: Cancellation stopped work before COMMIT or while waiting for another attempt.
fix: Respect the caller cancellation; start a new operation only under a new policy.

what: Work completed but the driver did not confirm COMMIT; writes may already be durable.
fix: Reconcile using an idempotency key or durable receipt; never blindly repeat the write.

what: PostgreSQL aborted every allowed attempt with a serialization conflict or deadlock.
fix: Shorten transactions or retry the operation later.

what: Transaction work or its driver threw an unclassified defect.
fix: Inspect the private cause and fix the failing implementation.

what: PostgreSQL explicitly rejected a statement or COMMIT, including constraint violations.
fix: Correct the write using the SQLSTATE; this does not imply a transient outage.

what: The driver could not execute the transaction because its connection failed.
fix: Inspect the private cause and restore database connectivity.
